jobs.title: Bookkeeper (Boekhouder)
jobs.description:
Bookkeeper (Boekhouder)

Monumental is automating on-site construction with robotics and software. Our mission is to make construction software-defined and autonomous - a future where beautiful, bespoke buildings go up in a single day, with minimal labour.

We're a growing team of engineers, operators and technicians from diverse backgrounds, including consumer tech, finance and media, and companies like Dyson, Shopify, Meta and Tesla. It's still the early days of building the company, and this is a chance to make an outsized impact on a problem that matters. From day one, you'll be working with an experienced founding team, backed by a $32M Series B led by Khosla Ventures and Plural, alongside other renowned investors.

Monumental is based in the city centre of Amsterdam, in a beautiful facility with a fully equipped workshop and robot testing floor. We build the whole stack in-house, hardware and software. Our work involves building robots in our workshop and houses on real construction sites, so we're onsite five days a week.

Read more on why we believe you should spend your time working on construction, and learn about our vision and company. You might enjoy our YouTube Channel, Based in Europe’s film on how we’re fixing Europe’s housing shortage, or this video by Andreas Klinger of what our office looks like.

About the role

We're looking for a Bookkeeper to bring our day-to-day bookkeeping and month-end close in-house. You'll be our first dedicated bookkeeper, taking over from our external accounting firm and running the books for our growing group: five Dutch BVs today, plus our entities abroad.

Our transaction volume has roughly doubled this year, and 2027 is the first financial year our accounts will be audited. You'll own the reconciliations, records and close process that make our numbers reliable, working closely with our finance lead, purchasing team and external accountants. The external accountants will continue to handle annual accounts and corporate tax, with local advisors handling tax filings abroad.

This is a hands-on bookkeeping role for someone with at least three years of experience running the full cycle through month-end. Our data and processes need cleaning up. If you enjoy turning a messy administration into a tidy one, this is that job. As you settle in, there is room to take on VAT filing and monthly payroll processing.

The role is based at our Amsterdam HQ, on-site five days a week. Salary is up to €50,000 gross a year, including the 8% holiday allowance.

What you'll do

  • Own daily bookkeeping. Code supplier invoices and card spend in Spendesk with the right GL account, VAT code and cost centre, and post them to the general ledger without re-keying. Keep supplier records clean and prepare payment runs. Supplier bank-detail changes are independently verified and approved; payment approval and release sit with the finance lead.

  • Keep accounts reconciled. Reconcile bank accounts, keep payables and receivables current, and investigate outstanding items so every balance is supported or explained.

  • Run the month-end close. Close all entities to a fixed timetable, initially by working day eight and moving towards working day five. Own accruals, prepayments and balance-sheet reconciliations, collect or prepare foreign entities' figures, agree intercompany balances and reconcile group reporting to the ledgers.

  • Maintain fixed assets and inventory records. Keep the fixed-asset register up to date, including capitalisation and depreciation of our robot fleet under agreed accounting policies, and reconcile inventory accounts to month-end stock values.

  • Prepare Dutch VAT returns. Prepare quarterly btw returns with our external accountants reviewing, and take over filing them over time.

  • Keep the books audit-ready. Maintain supporting schedules and an audit file throughout the year. Be a day-to-day contact for our external accountants and support the audit of our 2027 accounts.

  • Improve how we work. Document the close, fix recurring errors and use spreadsheets, software and AI tools to reduce manual work while checking the results carefully. Depending on your experience, take on payroll processing in Loket over time, with payroll tax filings remaining with our external accountants.

What we're looking for

  • Full-cycle bookkeeping experience. You have at least three years of experience running the books through month-end, at an accounting firm (accountantskantoor) or in-house.

  • Hands-on Dutch VAT experience. You've prepared Dutch btw returns and can work through the supporting records.

  • Strong reconciliation skills. You've handled balance-sheet reconciliations, accruals and prepayments, beyond processing invoices. You investigate differences and follow them through to a resolution.

  • Accuracy and ownership. You keep records organised, meet close deadlines and raise missing information or accounting questions early. You'd rather find the €12 difference than book it to suspense.

  • Fluent English and professional working Dutch. English is our working language, and your manager doesn't speak Dutch. You can independently read and process Dutch invoices, tax correspondence and payroll documents.

  • Comfort with systems and confidential information. You work confidently with spreadsheets, learn new accounting tools and handle financial and employee information carefully.

  • Nice to have: Twinfield, Basecone or Spendesk (Exact, Odoo or similar also counts); multi-entity or multi-country bookkeeping, intercompany and consolidation; fixed-asset or inventory accounting in hardware or manufacturing; statutory audit support; Dutch payroll experience, ideally in Loket; an accounting qualification such as MBO-4/HBO, SPD or Praktijkdiploma Boekhouden; experience automating repetitive work.

Why Monumental?

Joining Monumental means being at the forefront of a movement aimed at making significant strides in the construction industry. Here, your work has the potential to impact not just the company but the future of how we build. If you're driven by innovation, eager to tackle complex challenges, and ready to make a tangible difference, we want to hear from you.

For open applications (where you don't see an exact role match), please reach out to us at:

Unfortunately we do not currently support internships.

If you don't meet all the qualifications here but are excited about Monumental and feel you'd still be able to help us tackle complex challenges, do get in touch. We welcome generalists who focus on outcomes and are eager to learn on the job.

jobs.description:

With a global footprint spanning 134 countries, to date we’ve supported over 17,000 patients, 3,000 physicians and 350 sites, earning the trust of 60+ BioPharma companies. Salvo Software is a global technology company specializing in custom software development and advanced engineering solutions. With distributed teams across the US, LATAM, and India, we partner with clients to build high-performance, scalable systems that solve complex technical challenges. Our culture values innovation, ownership, and engineering excellence. We're growing our AI department and are looking for a hands-on AI Developer to help build it.

Role Overview

We are looking for an AI Developer to join and strengthen our AI department. Your core work will be building and operating LLM-powered systems: serving open-source models with Ollama and llama.cpp, building RAG pipelines, and developing MCP integrations that connect large language models to real tools and data. Solid DevOps fundamentals - Docker, CI/CD, Azure - support this work, but AI engineering is the heart of the role.

You don't need to be a deep ML researcher. What matters is production-grade Python, strong fundamentals, and the aptitude to learn fast. You'll work closely with our engineering and product teams to take LLM-powered features from prototype to reliably deployed systems, with mentorship available as you ramp up in areas like RAG architecture, Kafka, and advanced MCP work.

Key Responsibilities

AI / LLM Engineering (core focus)

  • Serve and operate open-source LLMs using Ollama and llama.cpp, locally and in on-prem environments.
  • Build and maintain RAG pipelines: embeddings, vector databases, chunking strategies, and retrieval quality.
  • Develop MCP (Model Context Protocol) integrations connecting LLMs to internal tools and data sources.
  • Build backend services in Python that power ML inference and AI-driven product features.
  • Parse and process structured and semi-structured data (XML/XSD, Office document formats) as pipeline inputs.
  • Grow into model optimization over time: quantization (GGUF), GPU/CUDA tuning, and offline/air-gapped deployments.

DevOps & Infrastructure (supporting)

  • Build and maintain CI/CD pipelines for AI services (Azure DevOps preferred; GitHub Actions / GitLab CI also used).
  • Deploy AI workloads to Microsoft Azure,AWS and containerize services with Docker.
  • Automate operational tasks with Python, Bash and/or PowerShell scripting.
  • Troubleshoot across the stack - dig into root causes rather than patching symptoms.
  • Support event-driven architectures using Apache Kafka (producers/consumers).
  • 3â5+ years engineering experience with production-level Python for building real services, LLM inference, RAG pipelines, and automated tooling.
  • Hands-on LLM & AI integration serving models via Ollama/llama.cpp, implementing vector retrieval/RAG, and developing MCP integrations (GPU/CUDA tuning & model quantization nice to have).
  • Cloud & Infrastructure expertise covering Azure/AWS deployments, Docker containerization, Linux/Windows admin, and CI/CD automation (Azure DevOps, GitHub Actions, or GitLab CI), with Terraform, Kubernetes, Kafka, or systems languages (Go, Rust, C++) as a plus.
  • DevOps, Security & Operations awareness, including Git workflows, scripting (Python, Bash, PowerShell), observability tools (Prometheus/Grafana), DevSecOps, and compliance frameworks (SOC 2, ISO 27001, Zero Trust).
  • Strong problem-solving & communication with a root-cause troubleshooting mindset, self-directed learning, strong ownership, and seamless remote/distributed team collaboration.

Joining Legora means three things.

  • We lean in: ownership over titles, outcomes over intentions.

  • We fight for excellence: high standards, direct, ego-free feedback.

  • We grow together: as a team and with our customers.

Mission before ego. Everyone contributes. No one coasts.

If you’re driven by impact, pace, and raising the bar. This is the place.

What you’ll be doing

Let's get the tricky part out of the way: this role doesn't fit neatly into a traditional box. It's part legal ops, part product specialist, part solutions architect, and part client whisperer. If you enjoy roles that stay static, this probably isn't it. Your mission is to help our clients, some of the most sophisticated tax and legal advisory teams in the world, get the absolute most out of our platform.

We are hiring for two of our teams. Our DACH team is focussed on working with Tax & Audit teams across the DACH market and our Benelux team is focussed on Tax & Audit teams across the Netherlands, Belgium and Luxembourg. Both are based out of our Munich office.

  • Acting as a thought partner to tax partners, legal advisory leaders, and consulting teams - building trusted relationships, addressing tricky pain points, and identifying high-value opportunities for them to scale their use of Legora across service lines and jurisdictions.

  • Working together with Go To Market and Customer Success in taking full ownership of client relationships - from running pilots with key practice areas, to onboarding new team members across tax, legal and consulting functions, and ultimately guiding firm-wide adoption across Big 4 and professional services firms.

  • Be the voice of tax and legal advisory users inside Legora - sharing insights from tax structuring teams, regulatory advisory practices, and legal consulting functions that directly inform product development, roadmap priorities, and strategic direction.

  • Delivering clear, confident product demos and training that bring the power of our platform to life - whether you're presenting to a tax partner, rolling out to a global advisory team, or training legal consulting professionals.

  • Documenting best practices from leading professional services firms, contribute to the development of scalable playbooks, and help shape how we grow this function globally.

  • Confidently helping tax and legal advisory teams navigate one of the biggest shifts in how professional services operate - from evaluating the ROI and competitive advantage of AI to clearly mapping how AI will impact different service lines, from tax compliance to regulatory advisory.

What you bring

You come from the world of tax and legal advisory; but you've never been content with how things have always been done. You may have trained at a Big 4 firm, working across tax structuring, legal advisory, or consulting. Perhaps you've specialised in legal operations, innovation, or technology implementation within a professional services environment. Maybe you've even moved into legal tech or consultancy, helping advisory teams modernise and scale. Either way, you know how tax and legal advisory teams think, work, and (sometimes) struggle and you're ready to help them level up with technology.

You'll thrive in this role if you:

  • Have a background in law or tax, with experience at a Big 4 firm or leading professional services practice gained in the DACH or Benelux market - ideally with exposure to multiple service lines, jurisdictions, or innovation initiatives.

  • Bring a fluent language skill relevant to the DACH or Benelux market (either German, Dutch/Flemish or French).

  • Are tech-curious and product-savvy. Not necessarily a coder, but passionate about navigating technical conversations, especially around things like generative AI, technology implementation, innovation and productivity.

  • Communicate clearly and confidently with diverse stakeholders, from tax partners to consulting leaders, and from lawyers to engineers. I.e. translating across disciplines is second nature to you.

  • Bring structure to ambiguity and energy to complexity; and enjoy being the calm, credible presence in a fast-moving environment.

  • Understand how to evaluate and improve existing processes as a direct result of new and emerging technologies - whether that's streamlining tax compliance workflows, enhancing regulatory analysis, or improving multi-jurisdictional advisory work.

  • Are proactive, self-directed, and comfortable juggling multiple client relationships at once.

  • Care deeply about quality, but don't get stuck in perfectionism - you get things done, and you make them better over time.

Spontaneous Application - Other Roles

About us

Owkin is an agentic AI company pioneering Biological Artificial Superintelligence to solve problems in biology where human researchers alone have failed.

K Pro is built on Owkin’s unrivalled multimodal patient data network, state-of-the-art AI for biology and a decade of experience working with pharmaceutical partners.

Not an engineer or a scientist? There’s still a place for you at Owkin.

We’re always glad to meet people who want to join us, whether or not a position is open today. We welcome spontaneous applications from profiles such as:

  • Business and partnerships: sales, business development, data and strategic partnerships, customer success

  • Product and project management: product managers, program and project managers, business operations

  • Marketing, communications and public affairs

  • Corporate functions: finance, legal, HR and talent, people operations, procurement and office management

You might be a good fit if you:

  • Believe AI can change how we discover and deliver treatments, and want to be part of it

  • Have a background in, or real curiosity about, pharma, biotech, healthcare or AI

  • Like working in a fast-paced, mission-driven environment where collaboration across teams is the norm

  • Are ready to learn quickly and bring your own ideas

What happens next:
If your profile aligns with a current or future need, we will contact you to arrange a conversation. Otherwise, with your consent, we will keep your details on file and reach out when a suitable opportunity arises.

What we offer

  • Flexible work organization

  • Friendly and informal working environment

  • Opportunity to work with an international team with high technical and scientific backgrounds

Recruitment Process & Security

  • Please complete the form and submit your CV.

  • Owkin is an Equal Opportunity Employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, sex, gender, sexual orientation, age, color, religion, national origin, protected veteran status or on the basis of disability.

  • Owkin is a great place to work. As a coveted workplace we are, unfortunately, vulnerable to recruitment phishing scams. We urge all job seekers and candidates to be wary of potential scams. Most of these have individuals posing as representatives of prominent companies, including Owkin, with the aim of obtaining personal, sensitive, or financial information from applicants. These scams prey upon an individual’s desire to obtain a job and can sometimes “feel” like a genuine recruitment process. Some red flags are identified below. Should you encounter a recruitment process that claims to be for Owkin but is not consistent with the below, please do not provide any personal or financial information:

  • Legitimate Owkin recruitment processes include communication with candidates through recognized professional networks, such as LinkedIn.

  • Communication is always through an official Owkin email address (from the @owkin.com domain), over the phone or through our applicant tracking system (Ashby).

  • The Owkin talent team do use platforms such as LinkedIn, however if you have any concern or doubt about this contact, please ask for them to send an email from @Owkin.com.

  • The Owkin talent team will not solicit personal data from candidates during the application phase including, but not limited to, date of birth, social security numbers, or bank account information;

  • Legitimate Owkin interviews may be conducted over the phone, in person, or via an approved enterprise videoconferencing service (Google Meets). They will not occur via Signal, Telegram or Messenger

  • Owkin offers of employment are based on merit and only extended once a candidate has interviewed with members of the talent and hiring team. Offers will be extended both verbally and in written format.

If you think that you have been a victim of fraud,

  • Check the identity of the talent team on LinkedIn

  • Check our senior team on our website https://owkin.com/team/

  • Check the existence of the position on our website: https://www.owkin.com/careers#current-opportunities

As our new Accounting Expert, you will lead core accounting operations while scaling our financial systems for sustained growth.

Your mission is to guarantee financial integrity, drive closing cycles toward a consistent, landing, and transform accounting into an automated, scalable machine.

jobs.title: Strategic Account Executive - Switzerland
jobs.description:
Strategic Account Executive - Switzerland

About ElevenLabs

ElevenLabs is an AI research and product company transforming how we interact with technology.

We launched in January 2023 with the first human-like AI voice model. Today, we serve millions of users and thousands of businesses - from fast-growing startups to large enterprises like Deutsche Telekom and Meta. Our investors are some of the world's most prominent, including Andreessen Horowitz, ICONIQ Growth and Sequoia. We've raised $781M in funding and our last valuation was $22B - multiples of 11, always.

We have expanded from voice into three main platforms:

  • ElevenAgents enables businesses to deliver seamless and intelligent customer experiences, with the integrations, testing, monitoring, and reliability necessary to deploy voice and chat agents at scale.

  • ElevenCreative empowers creators and marketers to generate and edit speech, music, image, and video across 70+ languages.

  • ElevenAPI gives developers access to our leading AI audio foundational models.

Everything we do is the result of the creativity and commitment of our team - builders doing the best work of their lives. We are researchers, engineers, and operators. IOI medalists and ex-founders. If you want to work hard and create lasting positive impact, we want to hear from you.

How we work

  • High-velocity: Rapid experimentation, lean autonomous teams, and minimal bureaucracy.

  • Impact not job titles: We don’t have job titles. Instead, it’s about the impact you have. No task is above or beneath you.

  • AI first: We use AI to move faster with higher-quality results. We do this across the whole company—from engineering to growth to operations.

  • Excellence everywhere: Everything we do should match the quality of our AI models.

  • Global team: We prioritize your talent, not your location.

What we offer

  • Innovative culture: You’ll be part of a generational opportunity to define the trajectory of AI, surrounded by a team pushing the boundaries of what’s possible.

  • Growth paths: Joining ElevenLabs means joining a dynamic team with countless opportunities to drive impact - beyond your immediate role and responsibilities.

  • Learning & development: ElevenLabs proactively supports professional development through an annual discretionary stipend.

  • Social travel: We also provide an annual discretionary stipend to meet up with colleagues each year, however you choose.

  • Annual team offsite: Each year, we bring your entire team together in a new location - past offsites have included Croatia, Italy and Cancún

  • Co-working: If you’re not located near one of our main hubs, we offer a monthly co-working stipend.

About the role

We're looking for an experienced, driven Strategic Account Executive to drive ElevenLabs' growth across Switzerland's largest enterprises. Our ideal candidate has a well-established network and a proven track record of selling to C-level and senior decision-makers at major Swiss brands and is passionate about the transformative possibilities of AI voice technology.

In this role you'll act as a strategic partner and trusted advisor, enabling clients to leverage our industry-leading models and ElevenAgents — our end-to-end platform for building and deploying AI voice agents — to reimagine their customer experience, internal workflows, and monetization strategies.

In this role you will:

  • Build and manage a growing portfolio of strategic accounts across Switzerland to help ElevenLabs meet its revenue goals.

  • Identify new business opportunities where ElevenLabs' conversational AI capabilities, including ElevenAgents, can drive customer engagement, contact center automation, and operational efficiency for consumer and retail brands.

  • Lead consultative, multi-stakeholder sales cycles, building compelling business cases that translate AI voice technology into measurable business value for senior executives and economic buyers.

  • Develop and maintain a deep understanding of the conversational AI landscape, including customer use cases, competitive solutions, and emerging trends, particularly as they apply to Swiss consumer and retail organizations operating at scale.

  • Demonstrate expertise, or a strong willingness to learn, about conversational AI and how ElevenLabs' voice technology can unlock value across customer support, virtual agents, IVR modernization, and in-app assistants.

  • Develop and execute account strategies to expand ElevenLabs' presence within the Swiss consumer and retail sector, navigating complex procurement and organizational structures.

  • Partner closely with Customer Success, FDEs and Solutions Engineering to ensure smooth onboarding, deployment, and expansion of accounts.

  • Serve as a trusted advisor to clients, educating C-suite and senior operations leaders on emerging trends in generative AI, voice interfaces, and conversational agents.

Requirements

  • 7+ years of quota-carrying strategic sales experience in SaaS or technology, ideally with exposure to AI, generative AI, LLM-based products, or API-driven platforms.

  • Proven success closing deals and managing long, complex sales cycles with multiple stakeholders across business, IT, legal, and procurement.

  • Well-connected in the Swiss consumer and retail landscape, with an existing network of senior individuals and strong executive presence and ability to build relationships at the C-suite and board level.

  • Experience selling technical solutions to product and engineering leaders; ability to translate complex technology into business value.

  • Deep understanding of enterprise procurement and legal processes in Switzerland, with the ability to accelerate deal velocity within complex organizational structures.

  • Comfort operating in an early-stage, high-growth environment, including building new playbooks and iterating quickly.

  • Passion for voice and audio AI and how it can unlock transformative value for customers.

  • A hybrid of customer and product-driven mentality that prioritizes client satisfaction and scale.

  • Swiss German is the preferred default language for this role; fluency in both Swiss German and French is a strong plus given Switzerland's multilingual market. Strong English is also required for internal collaboration.

Location

This is an in-country role based in Zurich.

We are an equal opportunity employer and do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, age, veteran status, disability or other legally protected statuses.

jobs.title: Superstar - Senior Art Director & Brand Designer
jobs.description:
Superstar - Senior Art Director & Brand Designer

International Brands ist ein schnell wachsendes Schweizer Unternehmen im Bereich Personal Care / FMCG. Mit unseren Marken bringen wir Produkte in zehntausende Verkaufspunkte weltweit, von Drogerien über führende Retail Chains bis hin zu E-Commerce.

Wir bauen Marken, die im Regal funktionieren.

Nicht nur auf Slides. Nicht nur auf Instagram.

Schnell. Sichtbar. Greifbar. Skalierbar.

Wir entwickeln und skalieren Marken, die Design, Produkt und Performance kompromisslos verbinden und genau dort gewinnen, wo es zählt: im Markt.

Über 90’000 Verkaufspunkte weltweit.

Und wir sind noch lange nicht am Limit.

Wir suchen einen Art Director (100%).

Keinen klassischen Designer.

Wir suchen den kreativen Kopf unseres gesamten Brand Powerhouses.

Jemanden mit einem klaren, tiefen Verständnis für FMCG Design. Jemanden, der weiss, was im Regal stoppt, Aufmerksamkeit gewinnt und Produkte verkauft.

Jemanden, der Verantwortung übernimmt. Von Packaging über Markenwelten bis hin zu den kleinsten Details, die am Ende den Unterschied machen.

Jemanden, der Bestehendes hinterfragt, Dinge besser machen will und nicht akzeptiert, „wie es schon immer war“.

Die Rolle ist anspruchsvoll, schnell und sehr hands-on.

Wir suchen keinen Verwalter.

Wir suchen einen Macher.

Jemanden, der Verantwortung übernimmt, Tempo bringt und Dinge mit hoher Qualität konsequent umsetzt.

Jemanden, der Marken aktiv weiterentwickeln will. Nicht nur konzeptionell, sondern bis zum fertigen Produkt im Regal.

Aufgaben

Du verantwortest alles, was unsere Marken visuell und kreativ nach vorne bringt – mit klarem Fokus auf FMCG Performance im Markt.

  • Entwicklung und Umsetzung kreativer Konzepte über alle Brands hinweg mit Fokus auf Sichtbarkeit, Wiedererkennung und Wirkung
  • Aufbau, Schärfung und Weiterentwicklung starker Markenwelten mit konsistenter Handschrift
  • Bestehendes hinterfragen, challengen und aktiv verbessern – nicht verwalten
  • Gestaltung von Packaging mit klarer FMCG-Logik: aufmerksamkeitsstark, markengerecht und mit Fokus auf Conversion am Regal
  • Entwicklung von Designs für Web, Social und Marketing Assets mit Fokus auf Performance statt nur Ästhetik
  • Ideen schnell, pragmatisch und effizient umsetzen – ohne sich in endlosen Abstimmungen zu verlieren
  • Aktiver Einsatz von AI und modernen Tools, um Workflow, Geschwindigkeit und Output kontinuierlich zu verbessern
  • Projekte eigenständig steuern und umsetzen – von der Idee bis zum fertigen Produkt im Markt
  • Steuerung von Freelancern und externen Partnern mit hohem Qualitätsanspruch
  • Enge Zusammenarbeit mit dem Head of Brands sowie dem gesamten Team
  • Blick fürs Ganze: vom Produkt über Kommunikation bis hin zum physischen Umfeld

Du machst aus Design Produkte, die verkaufen. Und aus Kreativität Performance.

Qualifikation

  • 2–5+ Jahre Erfahrung im kreativen Bereich (Design, Art Direction o.Ä.)
  • Starkes Portfolio mit echten FMCG- oder Retail-Projekten und sichtbaren Resultaten
  • Sehr gute Skills in Figma sowie Erfahrung in UI und Web
  • Erfahrung in Packaging, Social Media, Web und Print
  • Tiefes Verständnis für FMCG Design, Retail, Consumer Behavior und Kaufentscheidungen
  • Du hinterfragst Dinge und entwickelst sie weiter
  • Du denkst nicht nur in Ästhetik, sondern in Wirkung, Performance und Ergebnissen
  • Du arbeitest selbstständig, schnell, hands-on und lösungsorientiert
  • Du bringst Eigeninitiative mit und treibst Projekte aktiv voran
  • Du übernimmst Verantwortung statt auf Briefings zu warten
  • Du nutzt AI als sinnvolles Tool im kreativen Alltag
  • Deutsch & English

Was nicht zu der Rolle passt

  • Rein ästhetisches Denken ohne Verständnis für Markt, Konsumenten und Wirkung

jobs.title: Senior Manager Client Media (m/f/d) – Fixed-Term Contract
MSF International Managing Director
jobs.description:
MSF International Managing Director

Location: Based in Geneva or within approximately +/- two (2) hours from Geneva

Contract: Fixed term at 100% - It is a mandated role (currently 3+3 years)

Starting date: 01st of March 2027

Deadline to apply: 26th of November 2026 - We reserve the right to close this position once suitable candidates have been identified.

Compensation and Benefits: MSF practice is to offer the compensation and benefits package in line with the MSF entity offering the contract

*By default, the successful candidate will be offered a contract in the MSF office, able to issue a contract, of their country of residence at the time of application. If no MSF office exists in their country of residence, the successful candidate will be expected to relocate to a country where an MSF office can issue a contract, provided the local legislation allows for that.

At MSF, we are committed to an inclusive culture that encourages and supports the diverse voices of our employees. We welcome applications from individuals of all genders, ages, sexual orientations, nationalities, races, religions, beliefs, ability status, and all other diversity characteristics.

MSF is committed to preventing abuse, inappropriate behaviour, lack of integrity and financial misconduct in its work and care spaces. The successful candidate will be expected to comply with the organisation’s safeguarding policies and standards of professional behaviour.

We are committed to removing barriers for people with specific accessibility needs. If you need an adjustment to the recruitment process to be considered for the role, please let us know from the beginning of the selection process.

MSF International

Médecins Sans Frontières (MSF) is an international, independent, medical humanitarian organisation that delivers emergency aid to people affected by armed conflict, epidemics, healthcare exclusion and natural disasters. MSF offers assistance to people based only on need and irrespective of race, religion, gender or political affiliation. MSF International is the legal entity that binds MSF’s 26 sections, 28 associations and 16 branch offices together. Registered in Switzerland, MSF International provides coordination, information and support to the MSF Movement, as well as implements international projects and initiatives as requested.

I. CONTEXT

Médecins Sans Frontières (MSF) is an international, independent medical humanitarian organisation providing emergency assistance to people affected by armed conflict, epidemics, healthcare exclusion and natural disasters, based solely on need and irrespective of race, religion, gender or political affiliation.

MSF International is the legal entity whose membership is composed of all MSF associations. It hosts the International Secretariat, supports the International Board, facilitates coordination across the MSF movement, and provides shared services and initiatives as mandated by the movement.

Within MSF International, the International Office acts as the Secretariat of the International Board (IB) and operates under the direct management of the International Secretary General (ISG). MSF International also provides administrative and operational support to movement-wide initiatives and services, including MSF Access.

II. PURPOSE OF THE JOB

The MSF International Managing Director is a senior executive role responsible for institutional leadership, stewardship of resources, and organizational performance of MSF International as a legal entity serving the MSF movement.

The role ensures that MSF International:

  • Effectively implements -within the scope of MSF International - the MSF International Multiyear Plan and SPARC (MSF-wide Strategic Planning, Accountability and Resource Cycle) and supports the International Board and the International Secretary General in their governance roles and responsibilities.

  • Provides high quality, well governed services to the MSF movement, as mandated by the Full ExCom (executive committee);

  • Operates with strong systems of governance, accountability, risk management and duty of care;

  • Has robust, transparent and efficient governance, financial, human, and knowledge systems;

  • Operates as a coherent, inclusive, and accountable internationally distributed organization;

  • Models MSF values in leadership, equity, duty of care, and ethical management;

  • Ensures that the decisions taken by the Board of Directors of MSF International and its implementation is compliant with the Articles of Association, the internal regulations, as well as Swiss standards and Swiss laws, for as long as the registered office is in Geneva, Switzerland.

The MSF Management Director acts as a strategic partner to the International Secretary General, providing leadership on transversal and institutional topics with regards to the management of MSF International.

III. ACCOUNTABILITIES

1. Strategic Leadership and Implementation of MSF International (Multi‑year Plan & SPARC): Lead the translation of MSF International and movement strategic priorities into clear objectives, organisational plans, policies and resourcing within MSF International; support cross‑functional initiatives required by international platforms as needed to deliver the Multi‑Year Strategic Plan and SPARC commitments.

Expected result: MSF International delivers on agreed strategic priorities and SPARC commitments through coherent plans, measurable milestones and coordinated delivery across functions and movement partners.

a. Contribute to the development of MSF International Multi‑year Strategic Plan and SPARC within MSF International’s mandate and scope and translate strategic priorities into concrete organisational objectives, policies, systems and resource allocations, ensuring coherence across functions and services.

b. Supports cross‑functional and transversal initiatives required to deliver common strategic priorities and SPARC‑related commitments.

c. Contribute to movement-wide discussions on harmonization, efficiency and shared services.

d. Sets up and tracks implementation plans, including key milestones, indicators, and risks. Support the ISG in reporting to the International Board and relevant Standing Committees, and contribute to SPARC’s Monitoring & Evaluation Framework and Expense Steering Process for functions and services managed within MSF International’s scope.

e. Deputize for the ISG as required, within agreed scope and representation mandates.

f. Represent MSF International to key stakeholders, partners and external audiences as required, and build relationships that protect and advance MSF's institutional interests.

2. Governance, legal compliance, accountability and risk management for MSF-International: Ensure robust governance implementation, statutory compliance and effective risk management systems for MSF International as a Swiss legal entity and for services delivered on behalf of the movement; prepare governance-level advice and support Board decision-making.

Expected result: International Board and executive decisions are supported by timely, compliant and risk‑informed advice; MSF International statutory obligations and legal requirements are met and organisational risks are identified and mitigated.

a. Act as senior management liaison to the ISG, the International Board and Standing Committees on matters related to MSF International organisational governance, resources, risk, compliance and organisational performance.

b. Ensure robust systems of internal control, risk management and accountability, are in place and functioning for MSF International, in line with legal, fiduciary and associative obligations, including preparedness for critical incidents directly affecting MSF International.

c. Lead or support organizational responses to critical incidents directly affecting MSF International, including HR, legal, reputational, safeguarding or security‑related situations.

d. Ensure that MSF International fulfils its statutory responsibilities as a Swiss legal entity and that appropriate legal, administrative and governance support is obtained for decisions of the IB in light of the International Statutes, the Internal Regulations, and Swiss standards and law. Ensure compliance with applicable laws and regulations regarding daily management of MSF International.

e. Oversee compliance with GDPR and Swiss data protection law, promoting a culture of privacy and responsible data use.

f. Ensure appropriate legal review of all contracts and agreements directly involving MSF International and including those through which it delivers services to the movement, in accordance with MSF’s rules and policies, as well as Swiss law.

g. Design, implement and monitor the effectiveness of internal control systems and procedures; ensure that MSF International risks are identified and registered and ensure that mitigation measures are discussed and incorporated in the respective departments annual plans.

3. Services to MSF: Provide executive stewardship of movement-wide services mandated to MSF International, ensuring clear service governance, defined accountabilities and cost‑effective delivery.

Expected result: Movement services operate to agreed service charters and KPIs, with transparent costs and reliable delivery that meet sections' needs and contractual obligations.

a. Provide executive leadership and stewardship over services mandated to MSF International in support of the MSF movement, ensuring they are clearly governed, fit for purpose, cost‑effective and appropriately funded.

b. Ensure that roles, responsibilities, decision‑making authority and service boundaries between MSF International and MSF sections are clearly defined and communicated, balancing interoperability and mutualization objectives with the sections and ODs autonomy.

c. Establish and monitor service governance and performance frameworks, including service charters, KPIs, cost‑sharing arrangements and escalation mechanisms where relevant, and ensure transparency.

d. Facilitate structured dialogue with MSF sections to identify service needs, manage expectations and address risks or performance issues.

4. Financial stewardship and institutional integrity: Oversee budgeting, financial planning, statutory accounts, audits and financial controls; ensure alignment of resources with strategic priorities and manage institutional financial and insurance arrangements.

Expected result: MSF International maintains sound financial health, regulatory compliance and transparent resource allocation that supports strategic objectives.

a. Provide executive oversight of budgeting, forecasting and financial reporting for MSF International.

b. Ensure alignment between strategic priorities (including SPARC) and resource allocation.

c. Oversee statutory accounts, audits, financial policies and compliance with Swiss GAAP, tax and VAT requirements.

d. Oversee relationships with external auditors, financial advisors and legal counsel.

e. Oversee institutional insurance coverage and financial risk mitigation. Manage the full suite of institutional and corporate insurance coverage for MSF International.

f. Oversee legacies and donations earmarked for MSF International

5. People, culture and organisational development: Oversee people strategy, workforce planning, performance management, leadership development and organisational design to foster an inclusive, safe and high‑performing culture across a distributed workforce.

Expected result: A diverse, supported and capable organisation with clear succession pathways, strong performance management and a positive organisational culture.

a. Provide strategic leadership over human resources management, organizational design and workforce planning.

b. Ensure a safe, supportive, inclusive, equitable, diverse, respectful, and healthy workplace, free from abuse and other misconduct.

c. Oversee performance management, leadership development and succession planning.

d. Ensure a lively MSF International culture despite the geographical spread, including through adequate internal communication.

e. Lead organisational development, when necessary, to ensure the organisational structure remains fit for purpose and appropriate for a well-functioning office.

f. Manage institutional relationships with MSF sections hosting MSF International staff and ensure coherent frameworks for hosting, contracting, payroll and staff integration.

g. Ensure appropriate information governance and that knowledge management systems support collaboration, institutional memory and organizational learning, including learning from strategy and SPARC implementation.

h. Liaise regularly with the Staff Committee of MSF International.

IV. AUTONOMY, COMPLEXITY

The MSF International Managing Director operates with a high degree of autonomy to think, interpret and act within the strategic direction set by the International Secretary General, the International Board and the governance framework of MSF International.

The role is required to make independent judgements on organisational priorities, resource allocation, risk mitigation, service performance, people matters and operational responses, often in situations where issues are sensitive, cross-functional and without straightforward precedent.

The complexity of the environment is significant: the postholder works across a federated MSF movement with multiple stakeholders, distributed teams, hosted staff arrangements and diverse section interests, while also ensuring compliance with Swiss legal and regulatory requirements, internal governance rules, financial and HR procedures, safeguarding standards and data protection obligations. Success therefore depends on balancing institutional coherence, legal and procedural rigour, and service effectiveness with diplomacy, sound judgement and the ability to operate in ambiguity.

V. SAFEGUARDING REQUIREMENTS FOR THE ROLE

The incumbent commits to contribute to a safe, supportive, inclusive, equitable, diverse, respectful, and healthy workplace, free from abuse and other misconduct. They will not engage in any form of abuse including those detailed in MSF Typologies of Abuse and when an employee suspects or observes abuse, they will report it (without investigating it) to protect others.

  • Ensure respectful management and communication at all levels.

  • Ensure that staff and consultants under their supervision understand their responsibilities with respect to required behaviour and report abuse while working for MSF by reinforcing and regularly discussing expected standards of behaviour.

  • Welcome complainants, understand how to guide colleagues to appropriate channels, promote and create an environment that does not tolerate abuse or inappropriate behaviour. Guide colleagues to the correct process without investigating.

  • Ensure that staff know how to complain and keep staff updated on reporting mechanisms.


Education

  • Master’s degree in management, humanitarian affairs, political sciences, or a related field, or equivalent senior-level professional experience

Experience

  • Extensive senior leadership experience (General/Executive Director, Deputy Director or Director of a major organizational function) in a complex and large international and decentralised organisations

  • MSF experience is a major asset

  • Proven ability to operate at Board and executive level

  • Strong people leadership, including conflict management and change leadership

  • Solid expertise in financial oversight, governance and organisational systems

  • Experience with equity, diversity and inclusion strategies

Knowledge

  • Strong commitment to MSF’s humanitarian principles and associative values.

  • High level of integrity and ability to handle confidential and sensitive matters.

  • Knowledge of Swiss legal, institutional, employment, financial and data protection frameworks is an asset.

  • Familiarity with governance of associations and federated movements is an asset.

  • Proven ability to lead cross-functional and institutional change.

  • Comfortable leading teams across different locations and liaising with stakeholders at all levels.

  • Excellent written and verbal communication, able to communicate complex or sensitive matters clearly, concisely, and professionally.

  • High level of discretion, judgement, and emotional intelligence, and the ability to build a strong network across an organisation.

  • Confident decision‑making and the ability to act autonomously as appropriate.

  • Flexible team player, willing to adapt to changes, and confident tackling unfamiliar challenges across multiple domains of knowledge/experience.

Languages

  • Excellent English (written and spoken) is essential.

  • French highly desirable, and other MSF languages are further assets.

Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted.

By submitting an application, the job applicant confirms their understanding and acceptance of these recruitment procedures.

jobs.title: Process Safety Lead
jobs.description:
Process Safety Lead

About the role

As SkyNRG grows, we are looking for a Process Safety Lead to build and embed our corporate Process Safety Management framework.

In this role, you will set the standards for how process safety is managed across our projects and future assets, from design and construction through commissioning and operations. Working across Engineering, Projects, Operations and HSE, you will combine technical expertise with functional leadership to strengthen process safety across the organization.

Your key responsibilities include:

  • Develop and implement SkyNRG’s corporate Process Safety Management (PSM) framework as part of the Integrated Management System.

  • Establish and embed process safety standards and procedures across current and future projects, including construction, commissioning, start-up and operations.

  • Ensure compliance with SEVESO III requirements and support the Major Accident Prevention Policy, Safety Reports, regulatory inspections and audits.

  • Govern key process safety activities, including HAZOP, LOPA, QRA and Management of Change (MOC).

  • Develop and monitor process safety KPIs and barrier management to strengthen risk control and performance.

  • Lead process safety audits, incident learning and improvement initiatives across projects and assets.

  • Build process safety capability across the organization through training, guidance and functional leadership for Engineering, Projects, Operations, Maintenance and contractors.

Your profile

As a growing company in a rapidly evolving industry, we are looking for people who embrace change and are motivated to actively contribute to building and scaling our business. You are someone who feels comfortable in an entrepreneurial environment, takes ownership, and thrives when things are still developing.

You combine deep technical expertise with the ability to turn complex regulatory and risk-management requirements into practical standards. Structured and strategic in your approach, you are also willing to work hands-on to move implementation forward. You communicate clearly, make risk-based decisions, and can influence senior stakeholders without relying on formal authority.

You recognize yourself in the following:

  • A master’s degree in Chemical Engineering, Process Engineering, Process Safety, or a closely related technical discipline.

  • At least five years of relevant process safety experience within oil and gas, renewable fuels, chemicals, or another major hazard environment.

  • Practical knowledge of SEVESO III requirements and their application within Major Accident Hazard facilities.

  • Demonstrated experience developing or implementing Process Safety Management frameworks, Integrated Management Systems, or corporate process safety standards.

  • Strong technical expertise in HAZOP, LOPA, QRA, Management of Change, Mechanical Integrity, contractor management, and commissioning or start-up activities.

  • Experience assessing, governing, or assuring hazard studies across projects or operational environments.

  • A proven ability to design and deliver process safety training for multidisciplinary audiences.

  • Strong incident investigation skills, with the ability to translate findings into organizational learning and sustainable improvements.

  • The ability to influence stakeholders across Engineering, Projects, Operations, Maintenance, and site leadership.

  • Professional fluency in English.

  • Experience with digital risk-assessment or barrier-management tools would be an advantage. A recognized qualification such as MoSHE, NEBOSH Process Safety, or an equivalent certification is also beneficial. Direct experience engaging with regulators or contributing to SEVESO Safety Reports would make your profile particularly relevant.

About SkyNRG

Since 2009, SkyNRG has been a change maker in the aviation industry. We are dedicated to supplying and producing high-integrity Sustainable Aviation Fuel (SAF), making sustainable aviation a reality.

Collaboration is fundamental to achieving our ambition. We nurture genuine relationships with global partners in our drive to make SAF the alternative to fossil jet fuel.

Our in-house team of SAF experts have helped over 60 airlines and corporates reduce their climate impact using the Book & Claim mechanism; the most transparent and traceable way to support aviation sustainability with real emission reductions.

Sustainability is woven into the fabric of our company. We maintain an independent Sustainability Board, which advises the company on feedstocks and provides strategic guidance on wide-ranging sustainability issues. SkyNRG operations are certified against the RSB EU RED, CORSIA, and Book & Claim standards.

At SkyNRG, you’ll find:

  • An innovation-driven culture – where big ideas turn into real impact

  • Growth opportunities – in a fast-scaling, industry-changing company

  • A collaborative team – where your ideas and expertise are valued

  • A mission that matters – leading the change in the energy transition by producing and supplying high-integrity SAF

What we offer

We offer a brand-new office in the heart of Amsterdam, designed for collaboration and creativity. Most importantly, you’ll have the opportunity to contribute to a truly game-changing green initiative, making a real impact on the aviation industry and the planet.

Besides that, we offer:

  • 30 paid holidays + 2 for choosing sustainable travel options for your holidays

  • Contribute to a sustainable organization (B Corp)

  • Attractive bonus scheme

  • €5.000,- dedicated budget every 3 years for professional development

  • Commuting travel reimbursement + Lease a Bike plan

  • An office in the city centre of Amsterdam (Nieuwmarkt)

  • Work where it feels best for you: we offer flexible (hybrid in-office) working arrangements

  • Generous employer pension contribution

  • Paid Volunteering Day

  • Access to our electric company boat (also available for private use), free lunch, and lots of social activities – all part of the deal!

Is this you?

Are you ready to take the next step in your career with SkyNRG? Explore our vacancies and become part of our company of change makers. Together, we can change the future of flying.

For more information about SkyNRG visit www.skynrg.com.

📌 Please note: We do not accept sales inquiries or intermediary services.

At SkyNRG, we deeply value inclusion and diversity. As an equal opportunity employer, we are dedicated to ensuring every applicant has a fair chance, irrespective of race, color, religion, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, age, disability, or any other legally protected characteristics.

jobs.title: Creative Director
jobs.description:
Creative Director

Creative Director

Build with us

Businesses deserve better from finance. Less friction, more freedom. Since 2004, Mollie has been on a mission to make payments and money management effortless for every business in Europe.

Today, more than 250,000 companies trust our all-in-one platform to get paid, manage money and grow on their terms. Simple, scalable and built with real businesses in mind.

We’re one of Europe’s fastest-growing fintechs, with 900+ Mollies across 12+ locations. Our people make this growth possible. We move fast, build with purpose and care deeply about our customers. Whether you’re solving problems, building market-leading products or exploring how AI can make work smarter, you’ll have the freedom to create and the trust to deliver.

If you’re ready to grow, shape the future of fintech and join an ambitious, high-performing team, this is the place for you.

Your impact

As Creative Director, you lead and evolve Mollie's Brand Design function. You help define and drive our global brand design vision, keeping it consistent and excellent across every channel and market. You support the creative vision and execution of our brand across every touchpoint, from campaigns and product experiences to storytelling and motion. The job is to balance craft excellence with speed and scale.

Brand Design is a core enabler of our GTM and growth. You'll build a consistent, world-class brand experience across our platforms and markets, so the businesses we serve understand and choose Mollie. Your creative will power GTM and growth across Europe. We're a European business today, and going global is on our roadmap. You'll own the evolution of our visual identity, design systems and creative principles, and act as the quality bar for all brand output, with executive backing to shape how Mollie shows up everywhere, including as we expand.

You'll lead an in-house studio of around 5 to 8 designers across brand, motion, digital and campaign, and build a culture of craft, feedback and continuous improvement. You'll partner directly with marketing leadership, product, growth and our founder to turn strategy into insight-driven creative. You'll work with Marketing Operations on workflows and tooling, and bring in AI tools to speed up ideation, production and iteration without lowering the bar. You'll also collaborate with teams like Employee Experience and Internal Events, and manage external agencies, freelancers and production partners when needed.

What you'll ship

  • A clear, evolved brand design vision, plus a refreshed visual identity and design system that markets adopt consistently.

  • A high-performing, well-structured in-house studio, with the workflows, tooling and modular systems to deliver high-quality output at scale.

  • Impactful end to end creative for flagship campaigns, product launches and brand moments that is on-brand, insight-driven and effective.

  • AI-enabled creative workflows that measurably increase speed and output while holding the quality bar.

  • Strong creative partnership with Marketing, Product, Growth and leadership, including a meaningful uplift to performance marketing creative.

  • In your first 90 days: an assessment of the team, output and brand system, a defined vision and quick wins delivered.

  • Within 6 to 12 months: a scaled studio operating model, the evolved identity live in market and AI workflows embedded.

What you'll bring

  • Proven experience leading and scaling in-house design teams or creative studios, including people leadership of a multidisciplinary team. You inspire, challenge and develop designers at all levels.

  • A strong portfolio that shows high-quality brand, campaign and digital work, backed by proven brand craft.

  • Exceptional creative judgement and taste, and a clear point of view on what "great" looks like.

  • Experience building and maintaining design systems and brand frameworks that scale for consistency and self-serve.

  • Operational strength in planning, prioritization, resourcing and workflow design, so quality holds at scale.

  • Hands-on experience applying AI in creative workflows, including concepting, production and scaling assets.

  • Strong communication and storytelling, with the ability to explain creative decisions to senior stakeholders, and fluent English.

Grow your way

At Mollie, growth is personal. We believe everyone should have the chance to develop their skills, explore new challenges and shape their career on their own terms.

In this role, you’ll have the unique opportunity to build a meaningful distribution channel from the ground up. As we expand across Europe, you will grow alongside the product area you own. You’ll get regular feedback and performance reviews to support your development, with fair and transparent salary reviews along the way.

Unlock your full potential and join us to eliminate financial bureaucracy

If you're excited by the idea of building what's next, for yourself and for thousands of businesses across Europe.

Want a peek behind the scenes? Check out what life at Mollie is really like.

AI at Mollie

We believe in Always Be Shipping, and AI brings that philosophy to life across every team, every role, every day. AI is core to how we build. About ElevenLabs

ElevenLabs is an AI research and product company transforming how we interact with technology.

We launched in January 2023 with the first human-like AI voice model. Today, we serve millions of users and thousands of businesses - from fast-growing startups to large enterprises like Deutsche Telekom and Meta. How we work

  • High-velocity: Rapid experimentation, lean autonomous teams, and minimal bureaucracy.

  • Impact not job titles: We don’t have job titles. Instead, it’s about the impact you have. No task is above or beneath you.

  • AI first: We use AI to move faster with higher-quality results. We do this across the whole company—from engineering to growth to operations.

  • Excellence everywhere: Everything we do should match the quality of our AI models.

  • Global team: We prioritize your talent, not your location.

What we offer

  • Innovative culture: You’ll be part of a generational opportunity to define the trajectory of AI, surrounded by a team pushing the boundaries of what’s possible.

  • Growth paths: Joining ElevenLabs means joining a dynamic team with countless opportunities to drive impact - beyond your immediate role and responsibilities.

  • Co-working: If you’re not located near one of our main hubs, we offer a monthly co-working stipend.

About the role

We’re hiring a Product Manager to own the core ElevenCreative product experience for creators and marketers who sign up, subscribe, and build on their own. Self-serve users make up the majority of ElevenCreative’s user base, and they use the platform to generate and edit speech, music, image, and video across 70+ languages.

You’ll drive growth and adoption across the self-serve product experience, focusing on how users discover what ElevenCreative can do, how they move from a first generation into agents, video, and multi-step creative workflows, and what keeps them coming back and upgrading. There’s no shortage of things we could build. The job is defining the big bets, scoping them well, and shipping them quickly with the team.

PMs at ElevenLabs work in small, highly collaborative teams with minimal process, alongside engineers who have room to build creatively and lead. The scope is broad by design. Some weeks lean toward product, others toward growth or go-to-market work, and you’ll own whatever it takes to make ElevenCreative the best product for its users.

What you’ll do

  • Drive growth and adoption of the self-serve product, focusing on onboarding, activation, and upgrade moments, and partnering with growth, lifecycle, and pricing teams where they connect

  • Scope and define the big bets for the self-serve product across image, video, music, agents, and editing workflows

  • Find the biggest opportunities in the user journey through product data and user behavior, and turn them into clearly scoped projects

  • Drive adoption of newer experiences like agents and video, helping users expand from a single product into the full platform

  • Work with engineering and design to ship quickly, mocking up early concepts yourself when it speeds things up

  • Partner with growth, lifecycle, and social teams on launches and the moments that bring users into new parts of the product

  • Define success metrics for your area and track activation, engagement, retention, and conversion to paid plans

  • Talk to creators and marketers regularly to understand how they work and where the product falls short, and bring those insights back to the team

Requirements

  • 5+ years of product management experience on consumer or self-serve products

  • A track record of moving growth and adoption metrics through the products you’ve shipped

  • Deep familiarity with the creative space and the creators and marketers who use these tools, with a habit of bringing user insights into every product decision

  • Experience scoping and defining large, ambiguous bets and owning them end to end

  • Design-minded, with a high bar for quality and user experience and the ability to mock up concepts yourself

  • Technical fluency to go deep with engineers on how things are built and the tradeoffs involved

  • Strong analytical skills and comfort in product analytics tools to find opportunities and measure impact

  • A track record of shipping quickly and iterating based on what the data shows

  • Ownership pedigree, meaning you drive your own projects fully rather than handing off after the spec

  • Curiosity about AI and creative tools, and close attention to how the space is moving

Senior Field Marketing & ABM Manager, EMEA

Who We Are

Serval is the AI-native enterprise service management platform that automates the work legacy IT service management tools only track. Our AI agents build the automations that power employee support, then resolve requests against them instantly—helping teams across IT, HR, finance, legal, and beyond automate work within one governed platform.

Companies including Fox, Live Nation, Notion, Ramp, and Lucid Motors run on Serval. Headquartered in San Francisco, we’ve raised $277 million from investors including Sequoia Capital, Redpoint Ventures, First Round, General Catalyst, and Elad Gil, most recently a $150 million Series C at a $3 billion valuation.

We’re building a team that moves quickly, takes ownership, and wants to make a meaningful impact on how the world’s largest organizations work. Come help us build what’s next for enterprise service management.

Role Overview

The opportunities that matter most are often the hardest to get in front of. As our first Field Marketing & ABM hire in EMEA, you'll partner directly with Sales to build our field motion in the region from zero: high-impact programs across segments and 1:1 ABM plays for our most strategic accounts. You'll challenge the status quo in field marketing to create unique experiences and moments that open doors, build trust, and move deals forward.

This is a build role, not a run role. There is no EMEA playbook to inherit: you'll write it. Expect increasing scope, budget, and responsibility as our European presence grows, and expect to hire behind you.

Who You Are

  • Creative and opportunistic. You see an opening where others see a closed door. You know that breaking through to hard-to-reach accounts isn't about budget, it's about timing, creativity, and understanding what matters.

  • Allergic to "best practices" that produce mediocre results. You'd rather test something bold than execute something safe.

  • A doer, not a delegator. You're equally comfortable building a Salesforce report, negotiating with a venue in Shoreditch, or sending a llama with an invite around its neck to a CIO's office in Canary Wharf.

  • Comfortable being first. You're energised by an empty calendar and a blank budget line, and you don't need a US playbook translated for you.

What You'll Do

  • Define the EMEA go-to-market strategy for field programs: what we do, where we show up, and how we win across UK&I, DACH, Benelux, and the Nordics.

  • Design 1:1, 1:few, and 1:many field marketing experiences [regional dinners, happy hours, hackathons, out of the box experiences, etc] that align to active opportunities and target accounts.

  • Orchestrate ABM programs with Strategic accounts across channels: direct mail, events, digital, gifting, and content, navigating the practical realities of multi-country execution [shipping, VAT, GDPR, local vendors, language].

  • Partner with sales to understand territory priorities, account dynamics, and pipeline gaps, then actively participate in deal strategy, not just event execution.

  • Adapt what works globally and kill what doesn't travel. Bring the best of our US programs to Europe, and feed EMEA-born ideas back the other way.

  • Track impact through account engagement, pilots started, velocity, and closed-won revenue.

  • Create tight feedback loops with Sales leadership on both sides of the Atlantic to continuously improve territory strategy and program effectiveness.

  • Test unconventional tactics. Push boundaries. Try things that make people's jaws drop.

What You'll Need

  • 5-7+ years experience in field, experiential, growth, or ABM marketing.

  • Experience running programs across multiple European markets, not just the UK.

  • Proficiency with Salesforce, Hubspot [or similar], and intent tools [6sense, Demandbase, or similar].

  • Proven track record of running regional field programs, account-based campaigns, or growth programs that drove measurable pipeline and revenue.

Head of Internal Control, Operational Risk - CDI (F/H)

Lemonway est un établissement de paiement européen agréé, qui accompagne les marketplaces et les plateformes de crowdfunding dans plus de 29 pays.

Nous fournissons des services de paiement sécurisés, conformes et évolutifs pour la nouvelle économie, notamment des services de KYC, de traitement des paiements, de détection de la fraude, de ségrégation des fonds et de gestion des comptes. Notre expertise technologique et réglementaire permet à nos clients de développer leur activité tout en respectant les standards les plus exigeants en matière de conformité et de sécurité.

Avec plus de 150 collaborateurs, Lemonway est une entreprise dynamique et internationale, au cœur de l’économie numérique. Nous combinons l’agilité d’une scale-up avec les exigences et les responsabilités d’un établissement financier réglementé.


Le poste

Rattaché(e) a notre Chief Compliance & Risk Officer, vous prenez en charge les activités de contrôle interne, de gestion des risques opérationnels et de gouvernance de Lemonway.

Vous veillez à ce que le profil de risque de l’entreprise soit correctement identifié, évalué, suivi et communiqué, tout en contribuant au renforcement de son environnement de contrôle et de sa culture du risque.

Vous managez une équipe de deux personnes et travaillez en étroite collaboration avec le CEO, la Direction générale, les fonctions de contrôle et les équipes opérationnelles. En tant que véritable business partner, vous accompagnez l’entreprise dans ses prises de décision, tout en vous assurant que ses activités restent conformes aux exigences réglementaires applicables, aux politiques internes et à l’appétit au risque défini.

Il s’agit d’un poste stratégique et opérationnel, particulièrement adapté à une personne qui apprécie de construire et d’améliorer des dispositifs dans un environnement international, en forte évolution et réglementé.

Puisqu’il s’agit d’un poste centré sur la deuxième ligne de défense, nous recherchons des expériences en risques opérationnel et contrôle permanent au sein d’un établissement de paiement réglementé. Ce poste ne relève pas du contrôle financier, du FP&A, de la comptabilité, du contrôle de gestion ou du reporting financier.

Les principales responsabilités :

Contrôle interne et contrôle permanent

  • Piloter et améliorer en continu le dispositif de contrôle interne de niveaux 1 et 2.

  • Définir, maintenir et mettre en œuvre le plan annuel de contrôle permanent.

  • Veiller à ce que les contrôles soient correctement conçus, documentés, réalisés et justifiés.

  • Développer les indicateurs de contrôle pertinents et les reportings destinés à la Direction et aux instances de gouvernance.

  • Identifier les faiblesses du dispositif de contrôle, évaluer leur impact et coordonner les actions correctives.

  • Promouvoir une culture forte du contrôle et de la gestion des risques dans l’ensemble de l’organisation.

  • Contribuer à la mise en place et à l’optimisation des outils et processus de type GRC.

Risques opérationnels et gestion des risques

  • Piloter le dispositif de gestion des risques opérationnels, notamment l’identification, l’évaluation et le suivi des risques.

  • Coordonner la préparation et la mise à jour régulière des cartographies des risques de l’entreprise.

  • Organiser et maintenir le Risk Appetite Framework, ainsi que le suivi des indicateurs d’appétit au risque.

  • Piloter le processus de gestion et de reporting des incidents, en veillant à ce que les incidents soient enregistrés, analysés et suivis de manière appropriée.

  • Suivre les risques opérationnels, non financiers et émergents, notamment les risques liés à la technologie, à la cybersécurité, à la fraude, à l’externalisation et aux processus métiers.

  • Préparer des reportings risques clairs et exploitables à destination de la Direction générale et des instances de gouvernance concernées.

Gouvernance et comités

  • Préparer, coordonner et animer le Comité des risques trimestriel.

  • Accompagner le Chief Compliance & Risk Officer et la Direction générale dans leurs prises de décision liées aux risques.

  • Préparer les supports de gouvernance, tableaux de bord et présentations offrant une vision claire de l’environnement de risques et de contrôle de l’entreprise.

  • Coordonner la définition et la mise à jour des rôles et responsabilités, notamment au travers des matrices RACI.

  • Contribuer aux processus de reporting réglementaire et interne, notamment au rapport annuel sur le contrôle interne, ainsi qu’aux autres reportings réglementaires applicables.

Audits et contrôles réglementaires

  • Coordonner les audits externes, réglementaires et internes portant sur le contrôle interne, les risques opérationnels et la gouvernance.

  • Être le point de contact principal des auditeurs et des autorités compétentes sur les sujets de contrôle interne.

  • Gérer les demandes d’audit, la collecte des éléments justificatifs, le suivi des constats et les actions associées.

  • Coordonner la préparation et la mise en œuvre des plans d’actions correctifs et préventifs.

  • Suivre l’avancement des plans de remédiation et présenter les actions à risque élevé ou en retard aux instances de gouvernance appropriées.

  • Coordonner le programme de contrôle périodique et suivre sa mise en œuvre conformément au plan d’audit défini.

Externalisation, continuité d’activité et résilience opérationnelle

  • Garantir la robustesse et la bonne exécution du dispositif PSEE.

  • Contribuer au pilotage des activités externalisées et des prestataires tiers, conformément aux exigences réglementaires applicables.

  • Piloter les activités de continuité d’activité et de résilience opérationnelle de l’entreprise.

  • Maintenir et tester régulièrement les plans de continuité d’activité.

  • Participer aux exercices et aux réunions de gestion de crise lorsque cela est nécessaire.

  • Identifier les opportunités permettant de renforcer la résilience de Lemonway et sa capacité à maintenir ses activités critiques en cas de perturbation.

Politiques, procédures et formation

  • Évaluer les besoins de création ou de mise à jour des politiques, procédures, formulaires et documents de contrôle.

  • Coordonner la rédaction, la revue et la mise en œuvre des procédures de contrôle interne et de gestion des risques.

  • Concevoir ou contribuer à la création de supports de formation et de sensibilisation.

  • Veiller à ce que la documentation soit claire, opérationnelle, à jour et alignée avec le modèle de fonctionnement de l’entreprise.


Expérience

  • Vous disposez d’au moins 8 ans d’expérience dans le contrôle interne, les risques opérationnels, l’ERM, l’audit, la conformité ou un domaine proche.

  • Vous avez évolué dans un environnement réglementé, idéalement dans le secteur du paiement ou en fintech.

  • Vous avez déjà encadré une équipe et travaillé sur la structuration ou la transformation d’un dispositif de gestion des risques et de contrôle interne.

Compétences recherchées

  • Solide connaissance des dispositifs de contrôle interne et de gestion des risques opérationnels.

  • Bonne compréhension de l’environnement réglementaire français et européen, notamment des attentes de l’ACPR, des orientations de l’EBA, des exigences LCB-FT et de la DSP2.

  • Expérience du fonctionnement d’instances de gouvernance et de la préparation de reportings destinés à la Direction générale.

  • Maîtrise des environnements de transformation, de croissance ou de scale-up.

  • Expérience de la mise en place ou de l’évolution d’outils GRC.

  • Très bon niveau de français et d’anglais, à l’écrit comme à l’oral.

  • La connaissance de l’allemand ou d’une autre langue européenne constitue un atout.

Qualités personnelles

  • Leadership affirmé et bonnes compétences managériales.

  • Esprit structuré, rigoureux et grande capacité d’organisation.

  • Autonomie, tout en appréciant le travail collaboratif.

  • Approche pragmatique, orientée solutions et résultats.

  • Solides capacités d’analyse et grande attention aux détails.

  • Excellentes compétences en communication et en gestion des parties prenantes.

  • Capacité à challenger de manière constructive et à convaincre des interlocuteurs de tous niveaux.



Avantages
